entries.title: Promiscuity Opens Paths for Coevolution
entries.summary: Author(s): Naama Brenner Molecular “locks” that fit many “keys” may allow different plant mating strategies to coexist within a population of a single plant species. [Physics 19, 140] Published Mon Oct 26, 2026

entries.title: Single optical element combines soft X-ray imaging and spectroscopy
entries.summary: An international research team from Germany, Switzerland and Japan has demonstrated in a recent study that a single reflection zone plate (RZP) can perform both soft X-ray imaging and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) mapping. The approach could simplify future…

entries.title: Physicists reveal new paradigm for fiber growth in neurodegenerative diseases
entries.summary: Some proteins that are linked to neurodegenerative diseases can form both liquid droplets and amyloid fibers. But how are these two states connected, and where do the fibers grow? Leiden physicists Liru Feng and Louise Jawerth have discovered a counter-intuitive mechanism.

entries.title: Diamond defects confirm 80-year-old theory of crystal stress
entries.summary: For the first time, researchers in Japan have directly mapped several components of the stress field surrounding an atomic-scale flaw in the crystal structure of diamond. Led by Tokuyuki Teraji at Japan's National Institute for Materials Science, the team achieved its result…

entries.title: Tiny shifts in iron content tip a potential memory material between competing magnetic states
entries.summary: A team of Yale researchers has figured out what gives a magnetic material its mysterious properties, a discovery that could help boost computing memory and the field of "spintronics." Their work is published in Physical Review Letters.

entries.title: One extra quantum dot helps balance speed and stability in spin qubits
entries.summary: Quantum computers need qubits that can be controlled both quickly and reliably. Yet making semiconductor spin qubits faster often makes them more sensitive to electrical noise, creating a difficult trade-off.

entries.title: Curvature and cell mechanics control tissue organization
entries.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03496-w Tissue geometry mechanically regulates cell behaviour across scales. Now, it can be predicted when cells switch from full adhesion to rapid partial detachment on curved surfaces.
